A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPEED and retain matching methods and experiments. All 20 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices A–E, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original instance, artistic-style, celebrity and nudity-erasure experiments, component ablations and qualitative applications across diffusion models.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds adversarial evaluations, further baseline comparisons and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The core null-space update, IPF, DPA, IEC and value-only editing remain. v2 adds an adversarial training/editing adaptation, Ours w/ AT, following RECE (Appendix D.4); v1 discussed adversarial extension only as future work. The adaptation's exact procedure is not fully specified.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's I2P implicit-erasure evaluation, v2 evaluates MMA and Ring-A-Bell black-box attacks and UnlearnDiff white-box attacks (Appendix D.4). These introduce materially different adversarial test conditions. Existing instance, artistic-style, celebrity and MS-COCO coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 adds ESD-X, ESD-U, RACE and Receler to artistic-style comparisons; CPE, AdvUnlearn, RACE and Receler to implicit-erasure comparisons; and ConAbl and SPM variants to celebrity comparisons. SPM variants also gain MS-COCO comparisons. ConAbl and unedited SD v1.4 disappear from the reported implicit-erasure comparison (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 8).

E3.justification: Implicit-erasure reporting changes from body-part detection counts to ASR, retaining the NudeNet threshold of 0.6. Added experiments compare SPEED with/without adversarial editing and sweep the IPF filtering threshold. Figure 2's largest reported retain-set size changes from 30,000 to 20,000. Core sampling settings and few-concept/celebrity generation budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds adversarial robustness comparisons, an IPF filtering-scale sensitivity analysis (Figure 10a), and CLIP-scored case analyses (Figures 7–8). It removes v1's prior-shift profile (Figure 3) and prior-shift-versus-text-similarity ablation (Table 12). Component, edited-parameter and augmentation-count/rank ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and curves without uncertainty bands. Neither documents experimental repeat counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main SPEED benchmark scores are retained, but many baseline and adversarial results are added. Under the same reported three-instance setup, SPM w/o FT's Snoopy CS changes from 27.75 to 21.80 and retained Pikachu FID from 30.00 to 66.15 (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 5). MACE's 100-celebrity runtime changes from 1750.9 to 1736 seconds. I2P body-part counts are replaced by ASR entries, which should not be interpreted as same-metric performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 changes B_proj from V_r^T B to V^T B and replaces the justification for the positive constant c1 (Equations 27–31). This is a localized substantive proof revision. The revised Equation 30 remains unjustified when Sigma contains zero singular values, so it does not establish a valid repair of the lower-bound proof.

C1.justification: The central SPEED contributions and claim of erasing 100 concepts in five seconds remain. However, v2's introduction strengthens preservation from error 'close to zero' in v1 to 'zero' without affecting non-target concepts, a limited strengthening of the claimed guarantee.

C2.justification: v1 interprets SPM without Facilitated Transport as failing to erase multiple concepts; v2 instead emphasizes its poor preservation, consistent with revised results. v2 adds robustness–preservation–runtime interpretation and replaces the earlier adversarial-erasure limitation paragraph with limitations concerning nonlinear interactions, entangled concepts, abstract/culturally nuanced concepts, and larger or continual erasure settings.

D1.justification: v2 adds implementation-source links for ESD, RACE and Receler, but removes the k-means null-text compression disclosure, explicit 4,703-prompt I2P sample count, and ConAbl/MACE data-preparation requirements. Core SPEED hyperparameters and its code/model access statement remain. These documentation removals do not establish corresponding changes to the underlying procedure.

R1.justification: Related work expands to recent adversarial erasure and external/sampling safeguards, including RACE, Receler, AdvUnlearn, CPE, TRASCE and SAFREE, with additional discussion of open-source bypass risks. The central positioning relative to UCE, RECE and AlphaEdit remains, making this an extension of the existing positioning.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and null-space explanation. It moves implicit erasure from Section 5.3 to Appendix D.4, reorganizes supplementary experiments and further analyses, and adds ethics and reproducibility statements. The limitations section is also rewritten.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to predominantly one column. v2 merges the main few-concept tables, incorporates runtime columns into the celebrity table, replaces Figure 1's timing bars with a runtime–performance plot, and substantially rearranges application figures. Appendix tables expand, scored demonstration figures are added, and the sensitivity figure gains a filtering-scale panel.

improvement.justification: v2 directly evaluates previously omitted baselines and tests the adversarial extension left as future work in v1. Table 8 makes its trade-off measurable: adversarial editing lowers UnlearnDiff ASR from 0.75 to 0.45 while increasing MS-COCO FID from 37.82 to 39.51 and runtime from 3.6 to 4.5 seconds. This strengthens empirical support, but the net gain is limited by underspecified adversarial editing, lost reproducibility details and the unresolved Appendix B.2 proof gap.
